title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Center on 1973-03-28
lineage: Cassette Master -> Apogee MiniMe -> Samplitude Professional 8.01 -> FLAC/24

ai_review.summary: Stellar first set with a monster Dark Star captured on an audience tape that, despite some crowd noise, delivers an excellent performance.
ai_review.review: The concert dazzles in the opening half – Cumberland Blues, Here Comes Sunshine and a soaring 32‑minute Dark Star dominate, while the second set holds its own with Stella Blue, Eyes and Playing. Reviewers love Jerry’s expressive guitar tone (especially on Looks Like Rain) and Keith’s vintage volume‑pedal piano, though one listener complains about heavy Northeast audience clapping that colors the tape. The recording is an audience source; it remains clear enough to enjoy the music despite typical crowd ambience.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 5‑star praise for both performance and recording, but a single 0‑star review points to noticeable audience noise, creating some uncertainty.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear with good instrument separation; typical crowd ambience is present and occasional clapping can be intrusive but does not obscure the music.

poor_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider (interlude described as a ‘downward jam’)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is highlighted as killer and tightly flowing; second set is competent with a long Dark Star centerpiece, maintaining the show’s momentum despite a few less inspired moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar shines – expressive tone on Looks Like Rain, use of Crybaby wah‑wad adds extra color.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass is praised for its power in Dark Star (‘will split your atom’).
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano features a volume pedal that gives the vintage 1973 texture; keyboards are noted as inventive with limited effects.
